body:
## Summary

Adds a system for experimental gameplay features and lands the first one behind it.

- **Settings → Experiments**: a new settings category with one switch per experiment in the build (plus an explanation of what the page does). Off by default. Its sidebar entry uses Tabler's `flask` icon, added through the pinned icon manifest and exporter from #479 (the exporter regenerated every other icon byte-identically).
- **Baked into every new game**: the enabled set is copied into `GameHeader` when a game is created (custom lobby, map file from the load screen, headless `-test-games`, and multiplayer games the player hosts on YOG or LAN) by one helper, `Engine::applyLocalExperiments`, so saves, replays and every peer carry exactly the set the game was started with. Loading a save never applies current settings; joiners play with the host's set; a hosted saved game keeps its own set. **Campaign missions and the tutorial never take experiments**: scripted content plays as authored.
- **Stable keys, not bits**: saves, replays and the wire carry each experiment's kebab-case key. A key this build no longer knows is dropped on load with one stderr line (the agreed policy), so retiring an experiment never re-interprets an old file.
- **Visibility**: the custom lobby footer lists the active experiments; the multiplayer lobby panel and its Other options dialog show "Experiments set by the host" (the host now sends its header with the map, so joiners see it before start); the load screen names a save's experiments.
- **Headless**: every experiment key is a 0/1 rule in `GLOB2_TEST_RULES`; `--run-game` takes `--experiment <key>` and `result.json` lists the game's set under `resolved.experiments`.
- **First experiment, `guard-area-balancing`**: the simulation half of #265 re-applied by hand onto the current gradient pipeline (that branch conflicts with master) and gated at all four sites on `game->gameHeader.hasExperiment(...)`. Free warriors spread between painted guard areas by crowding, a bigger area gets more of them, and an over-full area trickles into the others. Design and numbers: `docs/features/guard-area-balancing.md`.

Five commits: the framework (with the first entry declared), the port, changes from an independent review (campaign exclusion, a single apply point, the crowding scratch moved into the per-slot gradient workspace and skipped when nothing is painted, a golden checksum trace proving the default path, string-table checks tying the registry to the catalogs, CLI coverage, and trimmed comments and docs), a rename keeping the guard-area test clear of Windows header macros, and the Experiments sidebar icon. Rebased onto master after #436 (the test revamp), #479 (icons) and #469 (Windows test fixes); the tests use #436's doctest binaries and fixtures. 

## Compatibility

- Save format **124** adds the experiments list to `GameHeader` after the custom-game rules (`FILE_FORMAT_VERSION_EXPERIMENTS`). Older saves load with no experiment; the `MINIMUM_VERSION_MINOR` floor is unchanged and the version 115 Maxima continuation fixtures still pass.
- Network protocol **47** (and the YOG floor): the header's wire format changed, so older clients are refused, as for the custom-game rule versions 31–33.
- `REPLAY_MINIMUM_VERSION_MINOR` stays at **123**: a format 123 replay loads with an empty set and the default simulation is byte-identical (evidence below).
- Preferences gain `experiments=<key>,<key>`; unknown keys are dropped there too.
- With every switch off nothing in the game changes. With `guard-area-balancing` on, `syncRand()` is consumed on a new schedule inside that game only.

## Verification (macOS arm64, release)

- `python3 test/run_tests.py --binary unit`: all pass, including the new `ExperimentalFeatures` suite (registry keys, text form, binary and text stream round trips, unknown keys dropped, corrupt count refused, `GameHeader` full and player-less forms, a version 123 header reading none) and the extended `GameHeaderTextSaveLoad` legacy truncation checks.
- `python3 test/run_tests.py --binary engine --no-display --exclude-tag map-generators`: 191 passed, 39 skipped (display), one failure that was the pinned protocol number in `TeamStatsSave`, updated to 47 and green on rerun. Includes `SettingsExperiments`, the new `CustomGameSetup` "experiments are baked in" case (lobby path, campaign path, save keeps the set after the setting is cleared, fresh mission then carries nothing), and the full `CustomGameSetup` lobby/replay case.
- `GuardAreaBalance` (10 cases): the **off** case reproduces the old outcome (spawn 24 / 0, nobody leaves) and matches a golden of the default game's per-100-tick checksums (`test/fixtures/guard-area/off-path-checksums.txt`, generated on macOS arm64 and matched by the Windows CI run); spawn and drain at all three refresh cadences, patches, size, three areas, erase, settled guards on six paint layouts, save/load continuation for 1,000 ticks, crowding box sum against brute force.
- `Settings` display cases at 640x480 (OpenGL, normal and expanded wording) run natively: the page renders, the `experiments.guard-area-balancing` toggle persists to `preferences.txt` and back.
- `scons release=1 server=1`: the YOG server links the registry.
- `python3 data/check_translations.py --strict`, `test/test_translations.py`, `test/test_font_coverage.py`: green with the six new keys in all 33 catalogs (machine-assisted, not native-reviewed).
- `test/tournament_cli_integration.py`: 20 main-binary cases pass, including `--experiment guard-area-balancing` (listed in `result.json`), an unknown key (`invalid_request`) and `--experiment` on a save (refused).
- `SettingsExperiments`: every registry entry's `[experiment …]` keys are listed in `texts.keys.txt` and match the English table; the feature's interface strings resolve.
- Headless smoke: `GLOB2_TEST_RULES=guard-area-balancing=1,scarcity=1` is accepted and `=2` refused; `--run-game --experiment guard-area-balancing` reports `["guard-area-balancing"]` and save version 124, `--experiment bogus` is an `invalid_request`.

Checksum sidecars (`GLOB2_CHECKSUM_SIDECAR=1`, `--nox <tick-0 state> 20000 1`, Warrush vs Warrush on SmallForTwo, `GLOB2_TEST_SEED=42`):

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Off path, tick-0 state written by the **base** build (format 123), replayed by base and by this branch | byte-identical, md5 `20f4f18c20f9f752255b894da2dfed1d` (80.3 MB, 12,226 ticks, same winner). A tick-0 state written by this branch (format 124) replays to the same game but its sidecar differs by exactly 2 bytes per tick (24,452 in total), the per-tick word that hashes the state's format version, so the like-for-like run above is the comparison that counts |
| On path (`guard-area-balancing=1`), this branch, twice | byte-identical, md5 `08a6a61ec46dc578ce43bd8cec4db437` (166.7 MB) |
| Off vs on | different games: the off game ends at tick 12,226 with a winner, the on game is undecided at 20,000, as #265 reported for its engine |

## Development measurements (guard-area balancing, from #265's harness, macOS arm64, seed 1)

Warriors at each area after 4,500 ticks:

| Scenario | Off (near / far) | On, every-tick refresh | On, ~10-tick refresh | On, ~170-tick refresh |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| spawn | 24 / 0 | 13 / 11 | 13 / 11 | 11 / 13 |
| drain | 24 / 0 | 11 / 13 | 11 / 13 | 11 / 13 |
| patches (two 3x3 patches) | 24 / 0 | 11 / 13 | 12 / 12 | 9 / 15 |
| size (5x5 near, 9x9 far) | 24 / 0 | 4 / 20 | 5 / 19 | 10 / 14 |
| three areas | 24 / 0 / 0 | 5 / 10 / 9 | | |

Guard-gradient rebuild (median of 200, two 5x5 areas): 64x64 map 31-32 us before, 36 us with 24 warriors after; 256x256 map 444-510 us before, 529-582 us after. Full step with 96 warriors: 181.9 us before, 70.0 us after (fewer blocked retries rebuilding the field). Settled-guard "no direction" share on the paint fell from 72-100 % to 0-24 % (1x1) and under 3 % elsewhere. A batch of 24 is 90 % inside some area by tick ~1,000 instead of ~250.

## Not verified here

- Cross-platform equality of the **on** path's long-game checksum sidecars: only macOS arm64 was run locally. CI builds and runs every suite, including `GuardAreaBalance`, on Linux and Windows (an earlier run on this branch passed all of this feature's cases on Windows, golden included); #265 recorded byte-identical sidecars on Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64 for the same mechanism on its unconditional branch.
- Android builds.
- Multiplayer end to end: the host/join wiring is the existing header messages, covered by the round-trip tests, not by a live LAN session.
- Multiplayer-hosted saved games keep the save's experiments; the pre-existing loss of the other custom rules on that path is unchanged and not addressed here.
- The settings page at 640x480 clips the last glyph of the experiment's help line by a few pixels. The info rows above wrap correctly, so this looks like the UI framework's small-font text measurement at the content edge rather than this page's layout; it is left for a framework fix.
- An in-game indicator of the active experiments is not included (the in-game menu is not on the declarative UI framework).

## Feel

With every switch off: no gameplay, art, pacing or balance change. With `guard-area-balancing` on (from #265): a batch trained together reaches its first area later (90 % in some area by tick ~1,000 instead of ~250) because part of it diverts; a packed area keeps its extra warriors milling beside it rather than frozen; an over-full area drains over a couple of thousand ticks, not at once; Warrush spreads its guard-area attacks across enemy buildings instead of massing on the nearest. This needs a maintainer playing it, per the review policy for gameplay changes.

title: Add experimental features with a settings page, baked into every new game; first one: guard-area balancing
